column2: Foreign Diplomatic Report: The Kingdom of Italy

A dispatch from Turin announces that Victor Emmanuel II has assumed the title King of Italy for himself and his successors. Following the plebiscites and the meeting of the first Italian Parliament, the House of Savoy now presides over the new kingdom. By retaining the numeral II, the sovereign affirms continuity with the Sardinian monarchy. Foreign cabinets must reckon with a new Italian power.

Our representatives report that a united Italian state has been proclaimed. The new government claims to speak for the territories brought together under its authority, replacing the former balance among the peninsula's states. Foreign cabinets now consider recognition and relations with the new power.
Take note of the Italian proclamation.
The proclamation of Italy must now be communicated abroad. Our representatives carry formal notice of the new state to foreign governments, opening a new chapter in its diplomatic relations.
The Former Papal Provinces Join Italy
The administrations of the former Papal provinces are brought under the authority of the Italian kingdom. The Sardinian offices complete their handover to the national government in Turin.
